```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 2](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop2.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the folder named under each heading. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk.

# [**NOTES**]{.underline}

If we start typing and we press tab it is going to continue typing what we wanted.

For example if i start typing *ass* and i press *tab* it is going to finish *assembly-stats* if that's the only option that it has.

If it has more options, for example, if we start typing *assembly-stats ass* and we press *tab* but there's a bunch of things that start with *ass*, we will have to press *tab* multiple times and it will show us the options that we have:

*assembly.fasta assembly_graph.gfa assembly_graph.gv assembly_info.txt*

and then we can chose the one we want.

If we try to type something that is not in our directory, it is not going to show anything.

If we want to access something that is not in the directory but in a folder of our directory we need to type the name of the folder and / and then the name of the file that we want to access. For example: *assembly-stats amtp4/assembly.fasta*
